If all three opposite pairs of sides are points of the unital, then this is a Triple O’Nan of the unital. More formally: Definition 1. In PG​(2,q2){\textup{PG}}(2,q^{2}), qq even or odd, consider a BM unital 𝒰{\mathcal{U}} with special point T∞T_{\infty} at infinity. A Triple O’Nan configuration is a set of six lines defined in the following way. Suppose there exists a quadrangle of four points in 𝒰{\mathcal{U}} such that, for the three pairs of lines partitioning the points of the quadrangle, each pair intersects in a point of the unital. These three pairs of lines forming six lines are a Triple O’Nan.
